# Introduction

This report documents the core data processing steps of the gDR-Incucyte pipeline.  Starting with the cleaned data from Step 1, this workflow converts the data into a standardized format and maps controls to treatments.

This step is critical as it maps control wells (e.g., DMSO) to their corresponding treatment wells. This file does **not** perform normalization. All normalization and growth rate calculations are handled in Step 3, based on the YAML configuration file for this run.

```{r libraries}
library(qs2)
library(MultiAssayExperiment)
library(data.table)
library(gDRutils)
library(gDRcore)
library(gDRplots)

```

# Key Output File

* **`gDR_data/gDR_mae.qs2`:** The main output of this step. This is a MultiAssayExperiment (MAE) object containing the processed SummarizedExperiment for the time-course data. This file includes all data assays (e.g., RawTreated, Controls, Normalized) and is the required input for Step 3: Analysis.

# Read Input Data

This section loads the cleaned and annotated `data.table` from Step 1 (`gDR_input.qs`), which contains all the merged information from the manifest, template, and raw Incucyte data files.

```{r drug_dose_layout}
wd <- "{{output_dir}}"
data_imported <- qs_read(file.path(wd, "gDR_data", "gDR_input.qs2"))
# Ensure it is explicitly a data.table
setDT(data_imported)

```

# Structure Data into SummarizedExperiment Object

This step converts the data.table into a SummarizedExperiment object. A key action here is the mapping of control data (e.g., DMSO-treated wells) to the appropriate drug-treated wells.

**Created assays:** `RawTreated`, `Controls`

```{r}
# Use the standard identifier from gDRutils for consistency
tc_type <- get_supported_experiments("time-course")
se_tc <- create_SE(data_imported, data_type = tc_type)

```

More information about this and the following steps related to the gDR pipeline can be found in the [gDR pipeline documentation](https://github.com/gdrplatform/gDRcore/blob/main/vignettes/gDRcore.Rmd).

# Normalize Viability Data

Normalized values are calculated with the Log2 Fold Change relative to Time 0 for every well.

**Created assays:** `LogFoldChange`

```{r}
se_tc <- normalize_SE(se_tc, data_type = tc_type)

```

## SE rowData

This table shows the metadata for the rows of the SummarizedExperiment, which correspond to the drugs and treatments.

```{r, create_SE_rowData}
generate_datatable(as.data.table(rowData(se_tc), keep.rownames = TRUE))

```

## SE colData

This table shows the metadata for the columns of the SummarizedExperiment, which correspond to the cell lines and experimental conditions.

```{r, create_SE_colData}
generate_datatable(as.data.table(colData(se_tc), keep.rownames = TRUE))

```

## Quality Control: Control-to-Treatment Mapping

This heatmap serves as a quality control check to ensure that every drug treatment in every cell line has a corresponding control value (e.g., DMSO) mapped to it. This mapping is critical for accurate data normalization.

**What to look for:**

* **Green Cells:** Ideal. This indicates a valid control was found.
* **Red Cells:** A problem. This indicates a missing control mapping for that specific drug/cell line, which will cause normalization errors.

```{r, create_SE_sa_qc, warning=FALSE, fig.show="hide"}
treat <- convert_se_assay_to_dt(se = se_tc, 
                                assay_name = "RawTreated")
controls <- convert_se_assay_to_dt(se = se_tc, 
                                   assay_name = "Controls")

# Calculate the frequency & create a heatmap
p <- heatmap_control_mapping_qc(dt_treat = treat, dt_controls = controls)

# create link to chart
txt_link <- create_zoom_link(
  file.path(".", "plots", paste("map_controls_to_treated", "{{viz_format}}", sep = ".")))

```

::: {.fullwidth}
`r knitr::knit(text = txt_link)`

```{r sa_controls, echo=FALSE}
print(p)

```

:::

```{r sa_controls_save, echo=FALSE}
save_plot(plt = p, 
          path = file.path(wd, "plots", "map_controls_to_treated"), 
          format = "{{viz_format}}")

```

# Assemble and Save Final Results (MAE)

```{r create_mae}
# Save using the standard experiment name ("time-course")
mae <- MultiAssayExperiment(experiments = setNames(list(se_tc), tc_type))
mae <- standardize_mae(mae)
qs_save(mae, file.path(wd, "gDR_data", "gDR_mae.qs2"))

```
